name: regex-redux
algorithm: Regex-redux workload over a generated FASTA DNA sequence (Homo sapiens + IUB sections): strip FASTA headers and newlines, count non-overlapping matches for 9 classic DNA alternation/class patterns, and perform 5 sequential IUB-style regex replacements with each language's std regex engine, folding all counts and sequence lengths into a checksum (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; there is no checked arithmetic to remove

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares standard library regex engines; folding the raw length, cleaned length, all 9 match counts and final length checks that every engine found the exact same matches and produced the exact same replacements
notes: All 15 regular expressions (header/newline cleanup, 9 classic DNA alternation/class match-count patterns, and 5 cascading IUB replacement patterns) are compiled once before the timed rounds.
Mk's std.regex and Go's regexp are RE2-style linear-time engines; C# uses System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex with RegexOptions.Compiled | RegexOptions.CultureInvariant and Regex.Count.
